title: A container can be told the smallest and largest it may get
goal: A group that hugs its contents can be given a floor and a ceiling, so a button with one letter in it is still a button and a card with a long title stops growing instead of running off the screen.
notes:
Comes from the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-04-ui-hug.json: "There is no minimum width, so a button with one letter in it is as narrow as one letter plus its room." Model lives in Sources/PhotonzCore/GroupLayout.swift, which today holds kind, direction, columns, gap, rowGap, padding, width and height and nothing else; usedWidth/usedHeight and hugsWidth/hugsHeight are the clamp points. Layout runs in GroupFlow.swift and the panel rows are in Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift. Keep the maths in the core, out of the view. Codable needs the new keys optional so old files decode.

Triage 2026-09-05: the 2026-09-04 runner was interrupted after writing its tests and before any implementation. It left Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/GroupSizeLimitsTests.swift behind, referencing GroupLayout.limitsWidth, limitsHeight and limitsSentence, none of which exist, so the whole test target could not compile and every task's test gate would have failed. The file is parked at queue/attic/2026-09-05-GroupSizeLimitsTests.swift.txt and removed from Tests. Read it for the shape it had in mind (a GroupSizeLimits value on GroupLayout, limits that survive a switch between Free, Stack and Grid, and a limitsSentence for the panel), then write the tests fresh.
acceptance: The Layout section offers a smallest and a largest size on each axis, empty by default, so nothing changes for a group nobody has set one on
A hugging stack never goes below its smallest size and never past its largest one, whatever is inside it
A stack pinned at its largest size lays its rows out in the room it has rather than overflowing quietly
The numbers survive save and reopen, and an old document with no numbers opens unchanged

Ships behind next-auto-layout. To see it: open Photonz Next, draw a rectangle, type a word on it, group them, set the group to Stack, turn Width to Hug, type 96 into the smallest width, then shorten the word and watch the group hold at 96
Tests cover the floor, the ceiling, both axes and the hug and fixed cases in PhotonzCore before the app code is written
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Discoverability: the Layout section already runs Arrangement/Direction/Width/Height/Gap/Padding, and Padding can open four more rows. Four more always-on rows for smallest/largest would be the section telling you it has run out of room, so the limits sit behind the same chevron idiom Padding already uses, on the Width and Height rows, and open themselves once a number is set. (2) The ui-autolayout mock does not draw min/max at all; this comes from a real audit line (a one-letter button is one letter wide), so there is nothing to copy and nothing to argue with. (3) Cut: no separate on/off switch, no per-child limits, no shrink-to-fit and no wrapping. Shortest version that delivers the value: four optional numbers on the model, one clamp, one extra layout pass only when a limit actually bites. (4) Collision found: a limit and a dragged handle. Dragging pins a size, so the ceiling has to stop the handle or the number and the box would disagree; tested. (5) Collision found: min above max. CSS's rule (the smallest wins) is the one people already carry, and typing 96 over a 9 passes through that state anyway. (6) Judgement call, no decision needed because it has no visible consequence a user would weigh: along the axis a stack FLOWS, spare room made by a smallest size packs at the near edge, exactly as a stack given a fixed width already does today. Spreading it would be the distribution control that was deliberately cut. (7) The button case is Free, not Stack, and a Free group leaves its contents where they were put, so a one-letter button held at 96 would have had its word jammed against the left padding. Fixed: on an axis a limit is holding open, the whole block of contents moves by the rule its contents agree on, so a centred label centres in the room the floor made.
runner exited without finalizing; reset to pending (attempt 1)
Triage: parked the interrupted runner's uncompilable test file to queue/attic and reset the task to a clean start.

Adversarial review before building, second pass. (1) The parked sketch's shape is sound: four optional numbers, not a nested value. (2) It got ONE thing wrong and the build fixed it: a ceiling that centres an oversized word pushes it off the NEAR edge into negative coordinates, where nothing else in the app looks for it. Contents too big for the room now start at the near edge and overhang the far one, which is what safe alignment means everywhere else. (3) Cut, as before: no on/off switch, no per-child limits, no shrink-to-fit, no wrapping. (4) Cut further during the build: limits on a screen. A screen's box is its own frame, a size somebody gave it, so there is nothing for a limit to hold, and the rows are hidden there exactly as Width and Height already are. (5) Discoverability: the limits sit behind the same twist-open Padding uses, on the Width and Height rows, and open themselves once a number is set. Four more always-on rows would be the section telling you it has run out of room.

Built. Core: GroupLayout gains minWidth/maxWidth/minHeight/maxHeight (optional, Codable keys optional so old files decode and untouched files write nothing), usedMin*/usedMax* reading them the same forgiving way as every other number, heldWidth/heldHeight/held(size) with the floor beating the ceiling, and limitsSentence for the panel. GroupFlow.holding works out the box the limits allow before anything is placed: an axis with a size of its own is simply held, a hugging axis is laid out once to find its natural size and only re-laid-out when the number comes back different, so a limit that does not bite costs nothing. GroupFlow.size holds its answer too, which is what makes Layer.localBounds agree without threading anything. closedAround's block shift became three cases, the third being the new one. LayerScaling.rearranging clamps the dragged box before it pins it, so the field and the canvas cannot disagree. setGroupLayout now carries a layout across a kind switch by changing only the kind, instead of listing the fields it kept, which is how the limits would have been forgotten.

Verified. 21 new tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/GroupSizeLimitsTests.swift written before any implementation, covering the floor and the ceiling on both axes, hug and fixed, stack and grid, the drag, the round trip, the old document, the kind switch and the sentence. Full suite green: 3225 tests in 279 suites. Walked live on the probe with Screen Recording granted (Scripts/playtest/size-limits-walk.json, 53 steps, all passed): a starter Button held open at 200 with its word centred in the room the floor made, stopped at 56 with its word overhanging, cleared back to None twice, and made 72 tall on the other axis. Real window captures, not offscreen renders.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real app. Kept: with both axes open the Layout section runs to twelve rows, which is a lot, but each pair is behind its own chevron and only opens when asked or when a number is set, exactly as Padding does. Kept: the Width row goes on saying Hug while a limit holds the box, because it IS hugging, with a floor, and the section's sentence says so. Left rough and filed: a word wider than its ceiling overhangs, because there is no way to wrap or shrink it yet (queue task words-that-outgrow-their-container-wrap-instead). Left rough, in the audit: a fixed width of 400 under a ceiling of 200 shows 400 in the W field and a 200 wide box.
Docs: a Landed section in docs/design/ui-building.md, including why the sketch's centring rule was wrong. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-05-group-size-limits.json with two real captures beside it.
